title: Global 32-byte reversal has minimum length 2 in the unary five-family AVX2 language
statement: Over single-register sequences drawn from permutation-control vpshufb, vpermd, vpermq, same-source vpalignr (imm 0..15) and identity/swap same-source vperm2i128, no one-instruction sequence reverses 32 distinct byte tags, and vpermd; vpshufb does it in two. The one-step formula is UNSAT -- and it is UNSAT by unit propagation alone, so the shipped DRAT is not load-bearing (see C.thm.vacuous-certificate).

formal.statement: axeyum_search::simd_synthesis::encode_unary_avx2_sequence(target=reversed, steps=1) is UNSAT; steps=2 is SAT with a replayed model.

scope: EXACT: unary single-register language {vpshufb (permutation controls), vpermd, vpermq, same-source vpalignr imm 0..15, same-source vperm2i128 identity/swap}; 32 distinct tags; no memory, no zeroing, no multi-source. NOT a claim about all of AVX2.

evidence.note: CNF regenerated from the prebuilt binary is byte-identical to the shipped one (SHA-256 7da5e266...). The checker accepts the shipped 957,982-byte CaDiCaL DRAT and correctly rejects an empty or junk proof -- but it ALSO accepts the proof with its first half deleted, because the formula is UP-refutable. The load-bearing certificate is therefore the CNF plus scripts/up_refutes.py, and the record says so.
Two-step model (vpermd dword reversal; vpshufb within-dword reversal) lifts and replays to the reversed tags (ADR-0566). Not re-run here.

sources: LLVM already lowers 32-byte reversal in two operations (X86ISelLowering.cpp); no published minimality claim

provenance.by: isa-calculus bootstrap (Claude Code session with axeyum)
